brief.headline: Part of this Data Engineer profile maps to work on this site, and part of it does not.

requirements.rationale: Duy engineered an ETL pipeline in Python — pandas, SciPy and h5py — converting five or more proprietary electrophysiology formats (XDPHYS .iid, .itd and .bf, MATLAB .mat, headerless CSV) into a single normalized relational database. The pipeline is end to end: it reads the raw lab files, applies the data-quality…

Duy drew and documented the boundary between data that belongs in Postgres and data that stays as committed JSON — data a stranger writes at runtime moves to the database, generated and partner-owned catalog data does not — so a fresh clone keeps rendering with no database at all. Duy designed the relational schema…

evidence.quoted_claim: Relational schema and ER model documented in LaTeX

requirements.rationale: Electrode depth has real provenance handling rather than an adjective about data quality: the raw instrument header records no usable depth for 143 of the 195 neurons, so the ETL falls back to the principal investigator's hand-curated position file and a depth_source column records, per neuron, which of the two the…

evidence.quoted_claim: Depth provenance recorded per neuron, not assumed
Data-quality rules written into the schema

requirements.caveat: This work is ongoing, so its counts move; every figure here was verified against the lab database on 2 September 2026 and is re-derivable from it.

requirements.rationale: Duy audited the whole team's pipeline output against the lab's eight stated file-naming and content requirements, and found 164 violations across all 16 date folders that had been uploaded. He traced the largest class of failures to a single line in the team's shared renaming notebook: its final loop hard-codes one…

evidence.quoted_claim: Root-caused to one hardcoded extension in shared code

requirements.caveat: The audit also reported the team's coverage honestly rather than favourably: 16 of the 36 required dates had been uploaded at the time, 44%, with 20 still to process.

The stack is Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, TypeScript in strict mode, Tailwind v4 with CSS Modules, Neon serverless Postgres, the Anthropic SDK with structured outputs, ONNX Runtime Web…

requirements.rationale: Duy has run the distributed stack, but as coursework rather than in production. In spring 2026 he took Big Data Analytics at Seattle University and built a two-stage Hadoop Streaming pipeline with a Hive query on top of it, on HDFS and YARN, and extended it into a TF-IDF search application on an EMR cluster. That is…

Airflow is part of the deployment work Duy is building right now, not part of anything he has shipped. What he has shipped is background jobs on Inngest in a production website, which is scheduling but not DAG orchestration.

brief.gaps_summary: This site does not fully evidence distributed data processing in production; orchestration in a shipped system. Each row above says which half is missing.
not_claimed: Not claimed: distributed data processing in production.
